boundaries.producer: authorized actor call, connection, message, or persisted alarm admission
boundaries.consumer: local actor runtime or celld actor turn
boundaries.carrierPlacement: synchronous in-process calls inherit the active runtime; generated workflow, agent, and processor callers capture one producer carrier for remote turns; alarm scheduling persists that exact carrier atomically with authority and input in local snapshots or celld Durable Object state; every admitted delivery links the carrier and records its one-based physical attempt while receipt replay creates no business boundary
boundaries.remaining: Prove the emitted gateway-to-celld path through live relocation and application-worker restart with collector-visible links; correlate explicit command-authorized alarm cancellation without misclassifying caller timeout as actor-turn cancellation.

boundaries.producer: authenticated agent invocation or parent managed execution
boundaries.consumer: generated agent worker and tool loop
boundaries.carrierPlacement: the authenticated Fetch gateway captures and forwards one framework-owned bounded carrier; the logical invocation durably retains the first carrier; only physical dispatch attempts create one linked agent boundary with synchronous provider-attempt and tool-operation children; join and replay create no business boundaries
boundaries.remaining: Prove a real provider/tool stream through emitted workers with restart, cancellation, redacted terminal outcomes, and collector-visible linkage; general callable-provider boundaries remain separate.

boundaries.producer: verified HTTP webhook, function-native issuance, or transactional event outbox
boundaries.consumer: generated Fetch gateway or admitted JetStream/Kinesis event-delivery worker
boundaries.carrierPlacement: verified HTTP ingress owns its external event boundary; transactional model execution captures its child carrier and persists it atomically with the event outbox; relay preserves that exact carrier; JetStream delivery count and the Kinesis checkpoint authority restore one-based physical attempts; the shared event executor validates and links the producer carrier, opens exactly one semantic event boundary per delivery, and drops malformed telemetry without changing business delivery; downstream processors own distinct linked processor attempts, while lakehouse publication remains an idempotent effect rather than a duplicate nested event span
boundaries.regression: bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 packages/applik8s/test/event-log-runtime.vertical.test.ts packages/applik8s/test/application-lakehouse.vertical.test.ts packages/runtime-nats/test/event-consumer.vertical.test.ts packages/runtime-aws/test/runtime.vertical.test.ts packages/compiler/test/application-lakehouse-publications.vertical.test.ts && bash scripts/run-v08-observability-postgres-live.sh && bun run test:v08:observability-generated-process-live
boundaries.remaining: The generated authenticated HTTP to PostgreSQL model/outbox to real JetStream lakehouse-publisher path now proves stable event identity, attempts 1 then 2 across publisher-process restart, one committed effect, redacted failures, local OTLP linkage, and verified cleanup. This does not qualify Kinesis as a live backend, a stream-processor attempt, a package-managed or external collector, ClickStack, or CloudWatch.

boundaries.producer: incoming Fetch or generated typed-HTTP request after route classification
boundaries.consumer: generated application gateway or typed-HTTP worker
boundaries.carrierPlacement: active runtime scope around the complete request gateway; workflow starts capture the child carrier before private-gateway admission
boundaries.remaining: The positive authenticated request-to-model-to-outbox causal vertical is proven in a generated process. Redacted denial, timeout, cancellation, and remote-provider failure outcomes remain.

boundaries.producer: managed transaction, durable command delivery, or nested operation
boundaries.consumer: native relational or Kubernetes model mutation
boundaries.carrierPlacement: PostgreSQL mutation attempts open after durable replay detection and remain active through handler execution, pre-commit authorization, authoritative state/history/outbox/result persistence, and typed rejection; ambient function-native transactions propagate deterministic database-retry attempts to nested model boundaries; generated Kubernetes creates open at the admitted gateway mutation seam and include idempotent conflict resolution
boundaries.regression: bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 packages/applik8s/test/transactional-database-postgres-runtime.vertical.test.ts packages/server/test/kubernetes-gateway.vertical.test.ts packages/compiler/test/application-fetch-gateway.vertical.test.ts && bash scripts/run-v08-observability-postgres-live.sh && bun run test:v08:observability-generated-process-live
boundaries.remaining: Deterministic and live PostgreSQL evidence covers authoritative commits, event outboxes, durable replay suppression, function-native nesting, intentional deadlock retry, and typed negative commit outcomes. Generated Kubernetes gateway evidence covers one admitted create boundary and idempotent conflict resolution. A live Kubernetes collector receipt may strengthen backend qualification, but is not required to keep the semantic model contract implemented.

boundaries.producer: authenticated transport or an active managed HTTP, workflow/task, transaction, agent-tool, or compiler-owned atomic execution
boundaries.carrierPlacement: authenticated gateway invocation owns the root operation boundary; compiler-generated HTTP and workflow/task scopes, ambient transaction-local model handles, and compiler-owned atomic handles open exactly one synchronous child around the actual call while preserving the operation contract identity through extracted handles and module-local helpers; AI tool execution retains its existing runtime-ai owner and is not wrapped again
boundaries.regression: bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 packages/applik8s/test/transactional-database-postgres-runtime.vertical.test.ts packages/compiler/test/application-fetch-gateway.vertical.test.ts packages/compiler/test/application-http.vertical.test.ts packages/operations/test/postgres.vertical.test.ts; NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 bunx vitest run --maxWorkers=1 packages/compiler/test/application-workflows.vertical.test.ts
boundaries.remaining: Deterministic runtime and generated-source evidence proves exhaustive maintained ownership, helper-mediated identity, synchronous nesting, and inherited redacted terminal semantics. A separate emitted-process collector receipt may strengthen backend qualification, but is not required to keep the operation contract implemented.

boundaries.producer: transactional outbox or broker event issuance
boundaries.consumer: stream processor attempt or frozen batch
boundaries.carrierPlacement: single-event and frozen-batch attempts link the internal stream envelope carriers with stable logical execution and explicit retry attempts; generated command and stream workers install the application-selected telemetry runtime and shut it down with the worker lifecycle
boundaries.remaining: Record delivery lag and redacted terminal outcomes, distinguish explicit replay, and prove an emitted stream-processor worker's PostgreSQL restart/cleanup continuity. The generated-process live receipt terminates in a lakehouse event publisher and deliberately does not qualify this separate processor boundary.

boundaries.consumer: one selected qualified provider operation invocation
boundaries.carrierPlacement: the framework opens one synchronous child only when the selected provider callable is physically invoked; provider discovery, qualification, placement, property access, and replay remain inert; direct application.inject() handles and compiler-hydrated static operations share the same boundary
boundaries.regression: bun run check:v08:provider-conformance && bun run check:v08:observability
boundaries.remaining: Prove a selected provider attempt in a real emitted worker and collector, including cancellation, timeout, retry, redacted terminal failure, and absence of arguments, results, credentials, and error messages.

boundaries.producer: authenticated query request or managed query invocation
boundaries.consumer: local or generated relational/Kubernetes query runtime and qualified nested query provider
boundaries.carrierPlacement: the public Fetch gateway owns only the HTTP transport for query routes; local relational and Kubernetes gateways create one semantic query boundary, each multiplex member owns one boundary for its complete iterator or watch lifetime, and internal invocations use the same identity. For remote queries the trusted root overwrites any caller-authored internal header with one bounded active carrier, the generated query gateway creates a child HTTP transport boundary, and the selected query runtime creates the semantic child. Lakehouse provider queries remain explicit nested logical query boundaries rather than alternate ingress ownership
boundaries.remaining: Prove the generated root-to-remote-gateway-to-query chain and multiplex cancellation against a real collector, including malformed carrier rejection, process restart, redacted failures, and verified cleanup.

boundaries.producer: kube-runtime controller admission from a resource watch, retry, or scheduled requeue
boundaries.consumer: one Rust host-owned reconcile attempt and its synchronous componentized-WASM guest
boundaries.carrierPlacement: the Rust host owns the only reconciler span, derives canonical operation/execution identity from the compiler runtime envelope, increments host retry attempts, and passes the exact span carrier synchronously into the guest; stale-generation status work remains a phase, replay creates no span, and unfinished host work closes as a typed interruption
boundaries.regression: cargo test -p applik8s-operator-host && bun run check:v08:observability
boundaries.remaining: kube-runtime does not expose whether a controller admission came from a watch notification or a scheduled requeue, so the host records the truthful bounded kubernetes-controller trigger rather than inventing provenance. Prove live watch, requeue, retry, trap, timeout, shutdown interruption, deletion/finalization, collector correlation, and restart continuity on emitted artifacts.

boundaries.producer: immediate caller or admitted provider occurrence
boundaries.carrierPlacement: active runtime scope around local and admitted schedule execution; durable provider carrier linkage still requires exact receipt evidence
boundaries.remaining: Persist exact producer context for future occurrences and prove retry, delayed delivery, provider scheduled time, cancellation, and replay semantics.

boundaries.carrierPlacement: generated task attempts validate the workflow producer carrier, create one asynchronous link with stable logical identity and explicit retry attempt, and propagate the active child carrier into task-emitted durable commands
boundaries.remaining: The OrbStack generated-worker receipt proves task retry attempts 1 and 2 link to the same workflow span across worker replacement, typed signal branches, cancellation, replay-safe effects, custom-CA OTLP export, redaction, and managed cleanup. Arbitrary external Hatchet service behavior remains provider-owned and unclaimed.

boundaries.producer: function-native call, HTTP start, schedule, signal, or parent workflow
boundaries.carrierPlacement: function-native calls and typed HTTP starts capture a validated producer carrier; Hatchet metadata persists it across a lost-response reattachment; generated workflow attempts restore it as one asynchronous link with stable instance and explicit attempt identity
boundaries.remaining: The OrbStack generated-worker receipt proves suspension/resumption, worker replacement, typed signals, cancellation, one Lease-fenced root run, retry-linked task attempts, custom-CA OTLP export, and managed cleanup without fabricating a second logical workflow span. Arbitrary external Hatchet service behavior remains provider-owned and unclaimed.
